To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the impact of interprofessional teamwork innovations on professional communication relationships and roles, and work satisfactions, in primary health care practices varies within and between countries, is influenced by local contextual factors, and is not entirely predictable.
the impact of reforms to interprofessional teamwork varied within and between countries and that this was influenced by the complexity of interrelationships within the practice.

Reforms seeking to enhance interprofessional collaboration in primary care practices are likely to have a range of positive and negative impacts, depending on local practice context and the capacity of practices to support interprofessional work."
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the impact of reform in primary health care (including interprofessional teamwork) on professional communication, relationships, roles, work satisfaction, and the health of the practice.
understanding the impacts of reforms on the work lives of practitioners, and the ways these are influenced by local context.
understanding how to create a better fit between reform and local contexts to improve outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impacts of reform on interprofessional teamwork are highly context dependent and that the impacts are complex and varied.
the impact of interprofessional teamwork interventions is complex and context dependent.

the impact of reforms on the interprofessional teamwork in primary care practices and on the work satisfaction of practitioners is complex and context dependent, with both positive and negative outcomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
interprofessional teamwork in PHC practices is complex, and that it requires a range of interventions and a supportive context.
there are many ways to create interprofessional practice in PHC.
the impact of reform interventions is highly dependent on the local context.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the impact of interprofessional teamwork innovations on professional relationships, roles, or work satisfaction is not entirely predictable and needs to be monitored and adapted at the local practice level.
the impact of reform on teamwork is highly context dependent and needs to be monitored and adapted locally to ensure positive outcomes for both the team and the patients they serve.
interprofessional teamwork is a complex phenomenon that requires attention to the context of the practice, including the size, leadership, and power dynamics.
